dialogue_script.speaker: Narrator
dialogue_script.text: The story is about a couple from New York who are returning home from a trip to New England. They are driving in a horse carriage, and are somewhere near Spiegletown when it starts getting dark and they have to seek shelter for the night.

dialogue_script.speaker: Wife
dialogue_script.text: George, I’m so tired that I can’t stay up longer. I want to lie down immediately.

dialogue_script.speaker: Husband
dialogue_script.text: Can you see that light through the trees? It must be a house. Let’s ride our horse quickly there.

dialogue_script.speaker: Wife
dialogue_script.text: Yes. Let’s do that. The night is as dark as hell! I’m scared.

dialogue_script.speaker: Narrator
dialogue_script.text: Soon, they reach a little house, and standing at the door, there is an old man and his wife smiling pleasantly.

dialogue_script.speaker: Wife
dialogue_script.text: Look at those people at the door. They are dressed in nightclothes. Do you think they can give us a room for the night?

dialogue_script.speaker: Husband
dialogue_script.text: Let’s ask. Good evening! Sorry for disturbing you so late. It seems that you are about to turn in. Do you think we could spend the night here? We are travelling as far as New York but it’s already dark.

dialogue_script.speaker: Old Man
dialogue_script.text: We are about to turn in, but please, welcome! You look so exhausted. Our house is not as luxurious as a hotel but it’s cosy.

dialogue_script.speaker: Old Woman
dialogue_script.text: Please, have a cup of hot tea and some cakes. They are freshly baked.

dialogue_script.speaker: Wife
dialogue_script.text: Thank you! Really, I haven’t tasted cakes as delicious as these before!

dialogue_script.speaker: Husband
dialogue_script.text: Please, allow me to pay you for the room and the food you are giving us.

dialogue_script.speaker: Old Man
dialogue_script.text: Oh, no! We could never accept money for a service as small as this! We consider you as our guests.

dialogue_script.speaker: Narrator
dialogue_script.text: The next morning, the travellers wake up early and get ready to leave the house quietly.

dialogue_script.speaker: Wife
dialogue_script.text: The bed is so comfortable that I can’t get out of it.

dialogue_script.speaker: Husband
dialogue_script.text: Very few people are as helpful as this couple. We can’t go without leaving them some money. Here, a fifty-cent coin! I’ll put it in the centre of the kitchen table. They can’t miss it.

dialogue_script.speaker: Narrator
dialogue_script.text: They get into their carriage and they go a few miles. They stop for a rest at a little restaurant in Spiegletown. The husband talks about the nice old couple to the owner of the restaurant.

dialogue_script.speaker: Owner
dialogue_script.text: Where do you say that house is?

dialogue_script.speaker: Husband
dialogue_script.text: On the hill, just outside Spiegletown.

dialogue_script.speaker: Owner
dialogue_script.text: You must be mistaken. That house was on fire. It killed the Brown family three years ago!

dialogue_script.speaker: Husband
dialogue_script.text: I don’t believe it! Mr. and Mrs. Brown are as alive as you and me.

dialogue_script.speaker: Owner
dialogue_script.text: Let’s drive back there quickly.

dialogue_script.speaker: Narrator
dialogue_script.text: There they find a burned out shell of a house. It is obvious that nobody can live in that place.

dialogue_script.speaker: Husband
dialogue_script.text: What’s that? That place can’t be the same! I must have missed the track.

dialogue_script.speaker: Wife
dialogue_script.text: Look! Look on the kitchen table!

dialogue_script.speaker: Narrator
dialogue_script.text: The husband looks into the ruins and there he sees a burnt table with a shiny fifty-cent piece lying in the centre.
